title: Precious Okoyomon transforms MoMA PS1 courtyard into living forest
summary: Artist and poet Precious Okoyomon (Nigerian-American, b. 1993) has transformed the MoMA PS1 courtyard into a living forest of plants, sculpture, and sound. On view from July 31, 2026 through 2028, Among the Flowers I Learned to Love: A Garden of Decreation (2026) is Okoyomon’s largest outdoor installation to date and the first of its kind in New York City, featuring a wild garden that evolves with the seasons and a giant teddy bear sculpture that visitors can enter and climb through. The installation inaugurates MoMA PS1’s Courtyard Commission series, a new biannual program inviting artists to create site-specific, large-scale works for the museum’s outdoor courtyard, reimagining how experimental art can transform public space. Accessible as part of MoMA PS1’s new free admission for all program, the installation invites audiences to experience the museum in new ways year-round, including during the Warm Up summer music series (Fridays through August 28). title: International art fair offers alternative for independent, experimental artists
summary: Artistic risk-takers, innovators and art lovers from around the world will gather in Torrance, California Aug. 7-9 for Tryst , an alternative to the established commercial art scene. The international fair and conference, now in its fourth year, invites experimentation, provides a support system for artist-run spaces and collectives and offers opportunities to purchase original artworks. Organized by the Torrance Art Museum in partnership with the City of Torrance, the free event will include performances and discussions about partnerships and programs for artists. title: First comprehensive monograph on artist Minjung Kim to be published
summary: Minjung Kim’s abstract works—the result of the patient manipulation of traditional Korean calligraphy ink and hand-dyed hanji (mulberry paper)—have garnered her global acclaim. Born in Gwangju, South Korea, Kim trained in traditional Korean painting before continuing her studies in Milan, Italy, where she developed a distinctive visual language at the intersection of Eastern sensibility and Western abstraction. Now based between France and the United States, she has cultivated a unique body of work that extends the possibilities of hanji, and has exhibited internationally for more than three decades. Minjung Kim: Ink, Paper, Fire is the first comprehensive monograph of the artist’s work, set to become the definitive text on her poetic, profoundly attentive practice. title: bg Fine Art presents The Strange World of Louise E. Marianetti (1916-2009)
summary: This August, bg Fine Art presents The Strange World of Louise E. Marianetti (1916–2009), an intimate exhibition of paintings from the artist's formative years of the 1930s and 1940s. The exhibition offers a focused look at Marianetti's highly personal vision within the broader tradition of American Magic Realism. Marianetti studied at the Rhode Island School of Design, graduating in 1936, before continuing her education at the Art Students League of New York under William Palmer and Robert Brackman. During these years she embraced the discipline of egg tempera painting while developing an artistic language that combined meticulous observation with quietly enigmatic subject matter. title: New cultural venue 'The Light' to open in Durham with major art exhibition
summary: Excitement is building for the opening of The Light in Durham on Saturday 22 August, the first venue in County Durham of its scale and remit dedicated to delivering contemporary art of national and international significance. Formerly the Durham Light Infantry (DLI) Museum and Art Gallery, the opening follows a significant investment by the venue’s owner, Durham County Council, and transformation by award-winning architects NORR. Bringing together contemporary art and creativity with local history, scientific discovery and technological innovation, The Light will explore the most important ideas of our time through an ambitious programme of exhibitions, events, immersive experiences and new commissions. The venue’s links to military history will be retained through a dedicated DLI Gallery telling the story of the historic regiment through objects, documents and film footage from the DLI Collection. title: Tony Hawk, Juice WRLD items head to auction in Julien's street culture sale
summary: Julien's Auctions announces “A Week of Street Culture,” a series of online-only auctions bringing together personally-owned pieces from Tony Hawk, Juice WRLD, and a curated selection of rare artworks and collectible skateboards. Over four days, collectors have the unprecedented opportunity to acquire 350 items at the intersection of sports, music, fashion, and design. Highlights include Tony Hawk's personally ridden and signed skateboard used during his professional career, the Jamie Thomas-ridden skateboard deck signed by Bob Dylan with lyrics to "Blowin' in the Wind," formerly the most expensive skateboard ever sold at auction, and performance-worn pieces from Juice WRLD in his iconic Rolling Loud and Lowlands Festival performances. title: Pair of rare Jacobite-era pistols reunited
summary: Two rare Jacobite-era pistols have been reunited in a new exhibition at Montrose Museum. A pistol on loan from National Museums Scotland is displayed alongside its pair in Tartan & Turmoil: The Angus Jacobite Story. The weapons date to the late 17th century and are rare surviving examples of work by the Montrose gunmaker and goldsmith William Lyndsay the Elder. The steel heart butt pistols are richly decorated with intricate floral engravings and silver mounts, stamped with Lyndsay’s mark. The pistols likely belonged to a wealthy and influential local family at a time when Montrose was renowned as a Jacobite stronghold. Following the failed uprising of 1715, it is believed the weapons were taken to France where they remained for over 200 years before returning to Scotland in 1993. title: Michael Zavros awarded Archibald Prize 2026 ANZ People's Choice award for portrait of Alex Ryvchin
summary: Acclaimed Australian artist and seven-time Archibald Prize finalist Michael Zavros has won the Archibald Prize 2026 ANZ People’s Choice award for his portrait Alex with his tefillin in the sea, a powerful work depicting Alex Ryvchin, Jewish community leader and Executive Council of Australian Jewry co-CEO. Voted by visitors to the Archibald, Wynne and Sulman Prizes 2026 exhibition, the ANZ People’s Choice award recognises the Archibald Prize finalist work that most resonates with the viewing public at the Art Gallery. This year, 45,769 people voted in the ANZ People’s Choice competition, which is the highest number of votes ever received in the award’s history. First awarded in 1988 and now supported by presenting partner ANZ, the award is one of the longest-running and most popular audience-voted art prizes in Australia. title: The Design Museum to open major exhibition of contemporary Black design this autumn
summary: This autumn, the Design Museum in London will open an exhibition guest curated by author and journalist Charlene Prempeh that charts the work of some of the most innovative contemporary Black designers working right now. The Nue Black Aesthetic — which runs from November 2026 until August 2027 — will feature 16 designers who are reshaping the design industry. It will be one of the most extensive exhibitions on contemporary Black design ever held in the UK. With over 100 objects on display, visitors will see innovative practices that span from fashion and furniture, to architecture, product design and sculpture. At the core of the exhibition will be the question: “What does it mean to be a Black designer working today?” Across six sections, the show will demonstrate that Black design is not a monolith, and that there is no single way to be a Black designer. title: Mexico City exhibition explores endangered Serbian medieval heritage in Kosovo
summary: More than seven centuries of Balkan history, faith and artistic achievement are at the center of Serbian Medieval Heritage in Danger, a temporary exhibition at Mexico City’s National Museum of World Cultures that examines both the beauty and the vulnerability of some of the region’s most important medieval monuments. The exhibition focuses on four religious sites in Kosovo: the Dečani Monastery, the Patriarchate of Peć, Gračanica Monastery and the Church of the Virgin of Ljeviš. All are inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List and have also appeared on the List of World Heritage in Danger for the past two decades because of political instability, regional tensions and the difficulties involved in protecting and monitoring the sites. title: National Portrait Gallery launches 'Artist Focus' programme with Issy Wood exhibition
summary: Today, the National Portrait Gallery launches a new contemporary programme, Artist Focus, offering a vital platform for artists expanding and challenging the genre of portraiture. The Gallery is delighted to announce Issy Wood as the first artist showcased as part of this new programme, which will offer fresh perspectives on how identity, representation, and human experience are understood through portraiture today. Featuring three presentations in the Gallery’s Weston Wing each year, Artist Focus – which is free to access – reinforces the Gallery's commitment to championing contemporary artistic practice, while fostering new conversations around portraiture's evolving role in art, society, and culture. title: Taiwanese photography exhibition explores the concept of 'Minjian'
summary: Rooted in research on Taiwanese photographic history, this exhibition revisits how “Minjian” became a crucial field of attention, intervention, and reflection for photographers across different generations. The decision to retain “Minjian” in Mandarin pinyin is part of the exhibition’s critical framework. Rather than translating it into “folk,” “vernacular,” or “popular,” the exhibition treats Minjian as a concept that must remain partially resistant to immediate equivalence. Within the historical contexts of Taiwan and East Asia, Minjian is therefore understood not as a fixed cultural category, but as a dynamic social space in which local networks, daily practices, religious life, publishing media, and the circulation of images continually intersect. title: 100 years after legendary theft, Grand Condé Pink Diamond goes on view
summary: From 17 October 2026 to 3 January 2027, the Musée Condé at the Château de Chantilly, in partnership with L’ÉCOLE, School of Jewelry Arts, presents an exhibition chronicling the history of a legendary historic diamond: the Pink Diamond. Known as the “Grand Condé”, the Pink Diamond is a historic gemstone weighing more than 9 carats, documented in the collections of the Princes of Condé since the 18th century. This jewel, exceptional in both colour and provenance, was stolen in October 1926 before being recovered shortly afterwards, hidden inside an apple. A century later, the Pink Diamond is once again on public display at this special exhibition. title: Houston Center for Contemporary Craft announces 2026-2027 resident artists
summary: Houston Center for Contemporary Craft announced its newest class of residents for 2026 – 2027, a group of 10 outstanding local and national artists working in craft media. For 25 years, the Center’s artist residency program has offered time and space for craft artists to focus on their creative work and interact with the public. The program supports emerging, mid-career, and established artists working in all craft media, including but not limited to clay, fiber, glass, metal, wood and mixed media. Residents are required to have their studios open for at least two days each week, giving visitors the unique opportunity to walk in, ask questions, and watch them work. This deeper level of interaction between artists and visitors allows the public to learn about a range of craft processes and techniques and helps artists gain exposure, make connections within the Houston community, and educate people of all ages about craft. title: National Gallery of Ireland to celebrate Jan Steen 400th anniversary with free exhibition
summary: 400 years after the birth of Jan Steen (1626–1679) – one of the leading Dutch painters of his time – the National Gallery of Ireland will host an intimate, FREE exhibition that looks at the variety of his extensive career. Jan Steen: Sacred and Profane will feature seven works by the artist from Leiden, drawn from the National Gallery of Ireland’s collection as well as important loans from the Rijksmuseum, Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, the Bredius Collection, the Bute Collection, and the National Gallery, London. Celebrated for his satirical and chaotic domestic scenes, Steen’s name is still synonymous in the Dutch language with a disorderly household. But during his prolific career he also produced history paintings, portraits and refined genre scenes. This exhibition will highlight the variety of subject matters, united by his lively and characterful approach to painting.

title: Fairfield University Art Museum earns national certification from AAMG
summary: The Fairfield University Art Museum (FUAM) is among the first museums in the nation to earn certification from the Association of Academic Museums and Galleries (AAMG), recognizing the museum's commitment to excellence as an academic museum serving Fairfield University and the broader community. The certification complements the museum's accreditation by the American Alliance of Museums and affirms the Museum’s dedication to nationally recognized standards in governance, collections stewardship, education, accessibility, strategic planning, and community engagement. The Association of Academic Museums and Galleries is the leading professional organization dedicated to academic museums, galleries, and collections in higher education. title: Sadie Barnette exhibition exploring family narrative opens at Joslyn Art Museum
summary: The exhibition Sadie Barnette opens in the Joslyn Art Museum’s Riley Contemporary Artists Project (CAP) Gallery August 1. Working across drawing, sculpture, photography, and installation, Sadie Barnette mines both personal narratives and collective histories, exploring how the two intersect and diverge over the course of one’s life. Her exhibition in the CAP Gallery centers on a recording she discovered on a doorbell security camera. In the short black-and-white video, the artist’s father is seen removing helium balloons from the trunk of a car. As he wrangles the inflatables—a gift for the artist’s mother—a single heart-shaped balloon floats away without his notice, prompting a bewildered search of the vehicle. title: Haggerty Museum of Art announces fall exhibitions
summary: This Fall the Haggerty Museum of Art at Marquette University will host three exhibitions and a full slate of free programs titled The Otherworld is Home. Inspired by the Yorùbá proverb, “Life is a journey, the otherworld is home” (Ayé l’àjò, ọ̀run n’ilé), the Fall season invites a journey across multiple centuries and continents through works from fifteenth-century Mali to newly created pieces by contemporary artists. Gallery talks, Community Day activities, and more will explore themes of shared human experiences, personal reclamation, cultural identity, spiritual passage, and connection across Africa’s many diasporas. Free and open to the public, The Otherworld is Home opens on August 28, 2026. title: The Met announces 2026-27 Live Arts season featuring St. Vincent and Jason Isbell
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art today announced its 2026–27 fall/winter season of Met Live Arts, which will feature world premieres as well as new commissions envisioned specifically for galleries at The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters as well as concerts in The Grace Rainey Rogers Auditorium. This also marks the inaugural season of programming by Sarah Jones, Lulu C. and Anthony W. Wang Head of Live Arts, who joined the Museum in 2025. Highlights of the upcoming season include performances by Lykke Li, St. Vincent, Jason Isbell, Kingfish, Ayodele Casel, and Rashaun Mitchell and Silas Riener, along with a series of holiday concerts at both The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters in December. title: ICA San José announces a major solo exhibition by Greg Ito
summary: The ICA San José will present To Give and Take, a solo exhibition by Los Angeles-based, Bay Area-trained artist Greg Ito, curated by Zoë Latzer. Opening September 18, 2026 and on view through February 21, 2027, the exhibition brings together new paintings, sculpture, and video installation that expand Ito’s distinctive visual language across mediums. The exhibition marks an ambitious new chapter in Ito’s evolving practice. Inspired by Shel Silverstein’s The Giving Tree, a story Ito first encountered as a child and now experiences through the perspective of a parent, To Give and Take reflects on how our understanding of love, sacrifice, and responsibility shifts across generations. Following the birth of his daughter, Ito began considering the ways families sustain one another through cycles of care, loss, and renewal.

title: Alison Bradley Projects announces U.S. representation of Alice Shintani
summary: Alison Bradley Projects announced the representation of Brazilian artist Alice Shintani (b. 1971, São Paulo) in the United States, in collaboration with Almeida & Dale, São Paulo. Alison Bradley Projects will present Shintani's first US solo exhibition in Fall 2027. Shintani's practice is grounded in an expanded understanding of painting as a site of spatial, social, and institutional inquiry. Working across painting, installation, collective actions, and interventions in public space, she investigates the ways images, objects, and gestures circulate between everyday life and the structures that frame contemporary art. Rather than treating painting as a discrete medium, Shintani approaches it as a mode of thinking—one that extends into architecture, urban space, and encounters with diverse publics. title: Photo Elysée and Rencontres d'Arles trace 200 years of animals in photography
summary: From scientific specimens and circus performers to beloved pets, endangered species and viral internet sensations, animals have occupied the photographic image almost from the moment the medium was invented. A major new exhibition, Modèle animal: 200 ans de photographie, brings together more than 500 photographs by 220 artists to examine how photography has shaped the way humans look at, live with, exploit and protect other species. Co-produced by Photo Elysée and the Rencontres d’Arles, the exhibition is on view in Arles through October 4, 2026, before traveling to Photo Elysée in Lausanne, where it will run from December 4, 2026 to April 4, 2027. title: First major exhibition of Lee Ufan in Portugal opens at Serralves this October
summary: Serralves Foundation will present Lee Ufan: Fragments of Infinity, the first major exhibition in Portugal of renowned South Korean-born painter and sculptor Lee Ufan (b. 1936). Set across the expansive 45-acre Serralves Park and the iconic Art Deco Serralves Villa, Fragments of Infinity explores the artist’s groundbreaking approach to blending natural landscapes with architectural environments. The presentation features three outdoor sculptures, strategically installed throughout the Park to frame direct encounters between stone, steel, and the surrounding environment. Inside the Serralves Villa, visitors will experience Lee’s meditative paintings — including a major new site-specific work. title: Patricia Low Contemporary in Venice announces new Mario Testino exhibition
summary: Patricia Low Contemporary, Venice announces the opening of a new exhibition featuring Mario Testino. Following his recent exhibition at Patricia Low in Gstaad, Mario Testino returns with a new body of work that builds upon his continuing exploration of beauty, identity and place. Just as his Gstaad exhibition reimagined the Swiss Alps through an idealised folkloric lens, this latest presentation is expected to offer a similarly poetic interpretation of Venice. Responding to the city's unique atmosphere and cultural legacy, the exhibition reflects Testino's fascination with photography as a medium capable of transforming both subject and setting into timeless, idealised visions.
